newsitem.title: USA: Washington Gas sets stock buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Washington Gas sets stock buybacks.

text.p: Washington Gas Light Co said Wednesday it will purchase up to 300,000 common shares in the open market to obtain the stock necessary to award each member of management 100 shares and provide for other potential awards on behalf of employees.
This purchase will represent less than 1 percent of the company's outstanding common stock, it noted.

In addition, Washington Gas said, the company is converting its dividend reinvestment and its defined contribution Savings and Capital Appreciation Plans from new issue stock to stock purchased in open market transactions.
The stock was awarded to management employees to support the company's announced intent to link financial performance more closely with compensation paid to employees, it said.

Although the company cannot unilaterally make a stock award to union-represented employees, Washington Gas said, steps are being taken to discuss with representatives of those employees how they can also share in the company's success.
For its fourth quarter, ended September 30, the company reported a seasonal loss of $0.43 per share, noting this compares to a $0.31 loss a year earlier.

The greater loss this quarter stems primarily from a portion of the estimated costs associated with a redesign of the company's organization, higher labor costs and the effects of the stock award to management, Washington Gas said.
For all of fiscal 1996, the company said, earnings per share were a record $1.85, representing an increase of $0.40 over 1995.

Washington Gas attributed the strong annual financial performance in large part to the unusually cold weather last winter which was nearly 25 percent colder than the previous winter. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
